findings.title: Team admin/owner check requires both admin AND owner
findings.body: isTeamAdminOrOwner is computed with && between isTeamAdmin and isTeamOwner, so a user must be both admin and owner to pass. A team admin who is not owner (or an owner who is not admin) is denied, and for non-team bookings teamId is 0 so the check is meaningless. The intent is clearly OR.

findings.title: Calendar attendees updated before the guests are validated/persisted correctly and with no error handling
findings.body: updateCalendarAttendees is awaited without try/catch, so any calendar provider failure makes the mutation throw after the attendees were already written to the DB, leaving the client seeing an error while guests were actually added. Also the handler uses the original booking object (before the new attendees) for eventManager, so calendar sync may not include the new guests.

findings.title: Email sent with raw input guests instead of the filtered uniqueGuests
findings.body: sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests) passes the full input list, including emails already attendees or blacklisted, and the evt attendees list includes all attendees. Newly added guests are identified by 'newGuests.includes', so previously existing attendees are sent 'scheduled' emails and blacklisted emails are not filtered; should pass uniqueGuests.

findings.title: Email failure silently swallowed with console.log, losing error details
findings.body: The catch block logs a fixed string without the error object, so email failures are invisible in logs. Should use the logger and include err.

findings.title: Guest attendees created with empty name and no check for duplicates within input
findings.body: Guests are created with name "" and duplicate emails in the same request are not deduplicated before createMany, so the same guest may be added twice. Also the check at line 76 compares raw guest to attendee.email without case normalization, so differently-cased duplicates are added.

findings.title: Organizer email subject uses first attendee name, not the new guests
findings.body: The subject in organizer-add-guests-email.ts uses this.calEvent.attendees[0].name, which is the original booker, while the email is about newly added guests; also the attendees array may be empty causing a runtime crash on [0].name.

findings.title: Crash when attendees array is empty
findings.body: this.calEvent.attendees[0].name dereferences index 0 without a guard; a booking with no attendees would throw inside getNodeMailerPayload.

findings.title: Mutation has no check that bookingId belongs to the caller beyond the handler; guests may be added to any booking
findings.body: addGuests uses authedProcedure and the handler checks only membership; the attendee check uses user.email on an existing booking and the team check is broken (see AND bug), so the authorization relies on the flawed logic above.

findings.title: Error toast message formatting is wrong
findings.body: The message is built as `${err.data?.code}: ${t(err.message)}`, which is always truthy, so the fallback t("unable_to_add_guests") is never used, and the raw error code prefix is shown to users.

findings.title: Zod schema recreated on every render
findings.body: ZAddGuestsInputSchema is defined inside the component body and rebuilt each render; it should be hoisted to module scope.

findings.title: Attendee email uses subtitle 'emailed you and any other attendees' that is inaccurate for newly added guests
findings.body: The subtitle text is reused from scheduled emails and the attendee is told they are receiving a calendar invite as in a new booking, but the email payload also sets status CONFIRMED and method REQUEST, which is a fresh invite for an existing event; behavior is questionable for existing attendees.
